title: Use sensitivity changes as a tool, not a threat
summary: If the player is plateaued and overly attached to one sensitivity, a deliberate alternate-sensitivity block can challenge stale movement patterns without erasing skill.
why: Aim improvement depends on adaptable mouse control more than preserving one exact setting forever.
A controlled sensitivity change can reveal whether the player is truly reading and controlling motion or just repeating one comfortable pattern.
actions: Run a short time-boxed block on a deliberately different sensitivity and compare control quality, not just comfort.
Keep notes on whether the alternate sensitivity exposes different arm, wrist, or finger weaknesses.
Return to the main sensitivity after the block and keep the useful movement cues that carried over.
avoid: Do not randomize sensitivity every session with no learning goal.
Avoid treating any temporary awkwardness as proof that the change was harmful.

evidence.claim: Sensitivity changes do not inherently destroy aim and can be used to improve adaptable mouse control.
